subject: physiology
title: Addison Disease, Conn Syndrome, and the Adrenal Medulla

steps.tx: Primary chronic adrenocortical insufficiency arising from autoimmune destruction of all three adrenal cortical zones is designated **Addison disease**. Because both glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid production are obliterated, patients present with profound fatigue, postural hypotension, weight loss, salt craving, hyponatraemia, and hyperkalaemia.
steps.say: Addison disease is autoimmune destruction of all adrenal cortical zones, causing fatigue, hypotension, and salt wasting.

left.title: Primary Adrenocortical Failure (Addison)
points: Autoimmune adrenalitis (anti-21-hydroxylase antibodies)
Destruction of cortex eliminates both cortisol and aldosterone
Loss of negative feedback produces massive ACTH elevation
Characterized by prominent cutaneous hyperpigmentation

right.title: Secondary Adrenal Failure (Pituitary)
points: Deficient pituitary ACTH secretion (tumors, Sheehan syndrome)
Cortisol deficiency with preserved aldosterone secretion (RAAS intact)
Plasma ACTH is low or undetectable
No cutaneous hyperpigmentation; normal serum potassium

steps.tx: Because cortisol negative feedback is abolished, the anterior pituitary secretes massive compensatory amounts of pro-opiomelanocortin, the precursor prohormone for adrenocorticotropic hormone. Proteolytic cleavage of pro-opiomelanocortin generates melanocyte-stimulating hormone peptide sequences that stimulate cutaneous melanocortin-1 receptors, producing the classic **hyperpigmentation of Addison disease**.
steps.say: High levels of the ACTH precursor POMC stimulate melanocytes, causing hyperpigmentation of palmar creases and mucosa.

nodes.label: Destruction of Adrenal Cortex Lowers Circulating Cortisol to Near Zero
Loss of Long-Loop Negative Feedback at Hypothalamus and Pituitary
Anterior Pituitary Produces Massive Amounts of Precursor Pro-Opiomelanocortin (POMC)
Co-Secreted Alpha-MSH and ACTH Stimulate Melanocytes -> Diffuse Cutaneous Hyperpigmentation

steps.tx: Acute decompensation of chronic primary adrenal insufficiency triggered by acute bacterial infection, surgical trauma, or abrupt corticosteroid withdrawal precipitates life-threatening **acute adrenal crisis**. Uncontrolled circulatory vascular collapse, profound hyponatraemic hypovolemia, hyperkalaemia, metabolic acidosis, and severe hypoglycemia require immediate resuscitation with high-dose intravenous hydrocortisone and isotonic saline.
steps.say: Adrenal crisis presents with refractory hypotensive shock, hyperkalaemia, and hypoglycemia, treated with IV hydrocortisone.

vis.alt: Acute adrenal crisis and cardiovascular collapse
vis.caption: Acute adrenocortical failure, mineralocorticoid shock, and emergency glucocorticoid resuscitation.

steps.tx: Autonomous, uninhibited hypersecretion of aldosterone by a benign adrenal zona glomerulosa microadenoma is designated **Conn syndrome**, or primary hyperaldosteronism. Excessive ENaC stimulation in cortical collecting duct principal cells induces persistent renal sodium retention, severe hypokalaemia, metabolic alkalosis, and treatment-resistant secondary arterial hypertension.
steps.say: Conn syndrome is an aldosterone-producing adrenal adenoma that causes hypertension, hypokalaemia, and suppressed renin.

left.title: Primary Hyperaldosteronism (Conn)
points: Autonomous aldosterone secretion by adrenal glomerulosa adenoma
Plasma Aldosterone Concentration (PAC) is high
Plasma Renin Activity (PRA) is suppressed (< 1.0 ng/mL/hr)
Elevated PAC/PRA aldosterone-renin ratio (> 20 to 30)

right.title: Secondary Hyperaldosteronism
points: Renal artery stenosis, congestive heart failure, or cirrhosis
Low renal perfusion pressure stimulates juxtaglomerular renin release
Both plasma renin and aldosterone are markedly elevated
Normal or low PAC/PRA aldosterone-renin ratio (< 10)

steps.tx: Remarkably, patients with Conn syndrome do not develop clinical edema despite continuous sodium retention, a phenomenon termed **aldosterone escape**. Expanding intravascular blood volume elevates mean arterial pressure and stretches cardiac atria, triggering atrial natriuretic peptide release and pressure natriuresis that stabilizes extracellular volume.
steps.say: Patients with Conn syndrome do not get edema due to aldosterone escape, where ANP and pressure natriuresis limit volume gain.

nodes.label: Autonomous Aldosterone Drives Continuous Principal Cell ENaC Sodium Reabsorption
Extracellular Fluid Volume Expands, Raising Arterial Blood Pressure
Atrial Stretch Triggers Atrial Natriuretic Peptide (ANP) Secretion
Pressure Natriuresis and ANP Restore Sodium Balance, Preventing Clinical Edema

steps.tx: The central core of the adrenal gland is the adrenal medulla, functionally representing a specialized sympathetic ganglion populated by **chromaffin neuroendocrine cells**. Innervated directly by preganglionic cholinergic sympathetic fibers from the splanchnic nerves, chromaffin cells synthesize, store, and release adrenaline and noradrenaline.
steps.say: Chromaffin cells in the adrenal medulla act like sympathetic postganglionic neurons, releasing adrenaline into blood.

left.title: Adrenal Medullary Secretion (~80% Adrenaline)
points: Synthesizes 80% Adrenaline (Epinephrine) and 20% Noradrenaline
Expresses Phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase (PNMT)
PNMT induced by high local concentrations of glucocorticoids via portal blood
Released as systemic hormone into venous circulation

right.title: Sympathetic Postganglionic Neurons
points: Synthesize and release Noradrenaline almost exclusively
Lack the PNMT methylating enzyme required for adrenaline
Released locally as neurotransmitter across microscopic synaptic clefts
Provides rapid, localized organ-specific autonomic control

steps.tx: Biosynthesis of catecholamines proceeds from tyrosine through L-DOPA and dopamine to noradrenaline. Within the adrenal medulla, high concentrations of cortisol arriving via intra-adrenal portal capillaries induce the enzyme **phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase**, which methylates noradrenaline into adrenaline, accounting for eighty percent of medullary catecholamine output.
steps.say: High cortisol concentrations induce the PNMT enzyme, converting noradrenaline into adrenaline in the adrenal medulla.

nodes.label: Tyrosine Converted to L-DOPA by Rate-Limiting Tyrosine Hydroxylase
DOPA Decarboxylase Converts L-DOPA to Dopamine in Cytoplasm
Dopamine Beta-Hydroxylase Converts Dopamine to Noradrenaline Inside Granules
Cortisol-Induced PNMT Methylates Noradrenaline to Adrenaline (Epinephrine)

steps.tx: A rare catecholamine-secreting neuroendocrine tumor derived from adrenal medullary chromaffin cells is designated **phaeochromocytoma**. Tumors oversecrete adrenaline and noradrenaline autonomously into the circulation, producing the classic paroxysmal triad of episodic pounding headaches, profuse diaphoresis, and tachycardia, accompanied by severe episodic or sustained malignant hypertension.
steps.say: Phaeochromocytoma is a chromaffin tumor causing paroxysms of pounding headache, sweating, palpitations, and severe hypertension.

vis.alt: Chromaffin cell tumor and catecholamine hypersecretion
vis.caption: Phaeochromocytoma chromaffin pathology, catecholamine surge mechanisms, and alpha-blocker therapy.
